name: Treaty with the Cherokee, 1816 (Treaty of the Chickasaw Council House)
nations: Cherokee (Tsalagi), today the Cherokee Nation, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians and the United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians
promises: Peace and friendship between the United States and the Cherokee (Article 1).
The Cherokee acknowledged a western boundary south of the Tennessee River and ceded the land south and west of it (Articles 2 and 3).
The United States would pay an annuity of $6,000 for ten years and $5,000 within sixty days of ratification for improvements on the surrendered land (Article 3).
The line would be marked by United States commissioners accompanied by two Cherokee appointees, with notice to the nation (Article 4).
The treaty would go to a Cherokee council at Turkey Town for approval; it was ratified there on October 4, 1816 (Article 5 and ratification note).
landTaken: Royce Area 79 in present Alabama, the land south and west of the Article 2 line.
compensation: $6,000 a year for ten years and $5,000 for improvements (Article 3). Payment was not traced.
today: No Indian Claims Commission or court ruling specific to this cession was found.

sources.title: Treaty with the Cherokee, 1816 (Kappler, vol. 2, p. 133)
sources.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Tribal Treaties Database

openQuestions: The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians settled Dockets 282-A to 282-L in 1972 for $1,855,254.50, a compromise covering its share of Cherokee cessions under treaties of 1785 to 1835 (28 Ind. Cl. Comm. 386). Whether this treaty was among the twelve dockets could not be read from the scanned 1959 severance order; even if so it would be a settlement, not a finding.
Unverified lead for a deeper pass: the relation of this cession to the 1814 Creek cession at Fort Jackson and to an earlier 1816 Cherokee treaty at Washington; no source on this was opened.
No account of this treaty by a Cherokee nation was found in this pass.
